citation.note: Payroll records (name, address, birth date, occupation, rate, hours, wages, itemized deductions, fringe benefits) kept at least 3 years (DWD 272.11(1)).
Pay frequency (§ 109.03(1)): wages paid at least monthly; logging and farm labor at least quarterly.

Final pay timing: regular payday or 24 hours on business separation: Employers must pay all wages on next regularly scheduled payday, or within 24 hours if employment ends due to merger, liquidation, relocation, or business closure (§ 109.03).

citation.note: Non-compete enforceability under reasonableness test: Governed by § 103.465; courts enforce if duration, geography, and scope are reasonable; blue-pencil doctrine applies (Runzheimer, 2015 WI 45).

citation.note: Mass Layoff Notice (§ 109.07): for employers with 50+ employees, flag mass layoff (25% of workforce or 25+ employees affected, whichever greater) or business closure (25+ employees affected) and enforce the 60-day notice requirement; validate recipient list (affected employees, unions, municipality). No severance mandate; notice only.

citation.note: Wisconsin Fair Employment Act prohibits compensation discrimination because of sex; no standalone equal-pay-for-equal-work standard separate from sex discrimination (§§ 111.31–111.395).

Pay statement itemization: employers must provide an itemized pay statement showing hours worked, rate of pay, and the amount and reason for each deduction (DWD 272.11(1); deduction reasons not coded without explanation).

Personnel file access twice per calendar year within 7 working days of a written request, at the worksite during business hours, for a reasonable copy fee; disputed information carries the employee's written position (§ 103.13).

Data breach notification (§ 134.98): any entity owning or licensing personal information must notify affected individuals within 45 days of learning of unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted personal information, unless the acquisition creates no material risk of identity theft or fraud.
